full_judgment:
The instant Rule is directed against the judgment and Decree dated 28-10-1993 (decree signed on 3-11-1993) passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Jamalpur in other Class Appeal No. 98 of 1987 affirming the judgment and decree dated 30-3- 1987 (decree signed on 23-6-1987) passed by the learned Munsiff, 1st Court, Jamalpur in other Class Suit No. 634 of 1980 dismissing the suit. 

 iv. Are the plaintiffs entitled to get a decree as prayed for? 

 7. He further submits that on proper appreciation of facts, and evidence on record, if it is found that material omission and non- consideration of facts and evidence has occasioned by the courts below, this revisional court retains authority to warrant interference to the impugned judgment and decree and to pass necessary order to give due relief to the plaintiffs. 

 8. He lastly submits that the impugned judgment and order warrants necessary interference and the suit of the plaintiffs be decreed. 

 12. He also submits that the suit was decreed by the 1st trial court by its judgment dated 30-5-1983 and against that judgment and decree there arose Other Class Appeal No. 58 of 1983 and the Appellate Court reversed the judgment setting aside decree passed by the 1st trial court and send back the case on remand to make necessary amendments but the plaintiffs did not take any step for amending their plaint and on proper appreciation of facts and evidence on record, trial court ultimately dismissed the suit and the Appellate Court as also a court of facts, on it’s independent assessment of facts and evidence on record and on proper observation affirmed the judgment passed by me trial court and since no material omission or misappreciation of facts and evidence or any error of law has occasioned in passing the impugned judgment, no reason appears to take any exceptional view against it. 

 16. On perusal of the record it appears that trial court decreed the suit by its judgment dated 30-5-1983 and the 1st Appellate Court set-aside judgment and decree that of me trial court dated 30-5-1983 by it’s judgment and order dated 15-7-1985 and send back the case on remand taking observation as under: 

 “As it appears, the High Court Division discharged the Rule on holding that the plaintiff/petitioners instituted the suit for a mere declaration that the disputed ewaznema deeds in favour of the defendant-respondent No. 1 is fraudulent and void whereas the respondent No. 1 contested the suit contending that the suit as framed was not maintainable and the pensioners had no title and possession in the land covered by the alleged exchange deeds; in the case of Md Jashimuddin vs Md Ali Ashraf reported in 1991 BLD (AD) 101= 42 DLR (AD) 289 it has been held that the plaintiff is not entitled to a simple declaration that the appellant’s kabala is false and fraudulent without first establishing his title to the suit land; in the case of Munsur Ali Malik vs Md Nurul Hoque Mallik reported in 1986 BCR (AD) 58 the  High Court Division dismissed the suit on  the ground that the defendant in the suit  having challenged the possession of the plaintiff, it was incumbent upon the  plaintiff to file regular suit for declaration  of title and confirmation of possession and  the suit is not maintainable for his failure to  ask consequential relief, and in the case of  Sahara Khatun vs Anowara Khatun reported  in 1 BCR 126 it has been held that before the plaintiff can be given a declaration that a decree or kabala is fraudulent and not binding upon her, it is not enough for he just to make out a prima facie case that she has right title and interest in the suit property but she has no prove that she had the legal character or the right to property she claimed and unless she could prove such legal character or right to property she could not be given any such declaratory relief and the facts and circumstances of the above reported cases being similar to the facts and circumstances of the present case, the principle laid down therein are applicable in the present case and accordingly, the petitioners ought to have filed a suit for declaration of title and partition of the suit land.” 

 “1 am ready to pay the mortgage money if the suit is decreed”
